name: Foundation-prior stereo: FoundationStereo, Fast-FoundationStereo, DEFOM-Stereo, MonSter (and MonSter++)
authors_org: FoundationStereo: Bowen Wen, Matthew Trepte, Joseph Aribido, Jan Kautz, Orazio Gallo, Stan Birchfield (NVIDIA). Fast-FoundationStereo: Bowen Wen, Shaurya Dewan, Stan Birchfield (NVIDIA). DEFOM-Stereo: Hualie Jiang, Zhiqiang Lou, Laiyan Ding, Rui Xu, Minglang Tan, Wenjie Jiang, Rui Huang (CUHK-Shenzhen / Insta360). MonSter: Junda Cheng et al. (Huazhong Univ. of Science and Technology and collaborators).
year: 2025 (FoundationStereo, DEFOM-Stereo, MonSter: CVPR 2025); Fast-FoundationStereo arXiv Dec 2025; MonSter++ arXiv 2025
venue_link: FoundationStereo CVPR 2025 oral, best-paper nomination: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09898 , https://nvlabs.github.io/FoundationStereo/ ; Fast-FoundationStereo: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11130 , https://nvlabs.github.io/Fast-FoundationStereo/ ; DEFOM-Stereo CVPR 2025: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09466 ; MonSter CVPR 2025 highlight: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/html/Cheng_MonSter_Marry_Monodepth_to_Stereo_Unleashes_Power_CVPR_2025_paper.html ; MonSter++: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.08643
code_availability: FoundationStereo: code and weights at https://github.com/NVlabs/FoundationStereo (NVIDIA license, non-commercial). DEFOM-Stereo: code and checkpoints at https://github.com/Insta360-Research-Team/DEFOM-Stereo . MonSter: https://github.com/Junda24/MonSter . Fast-FoundationStereo: the v1 paper says code, models and pseudo-labels will be released upon acceptance [uncertain] whether they are released yet. None of the weights transfer here: all are RGB photo models, and our input is a 16-channel synthetic cost image.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (CVPR 2025) for FoundationStereo, DEFOM-Stereo and MonSter; arXiv preprint for Fast-FoundationStereo and MonSter++. Details read from the arXiv HTML versions. The CVF PDFs for DEFOM and MonSter returned 403, so some MonSter ablation numbers come from the MonSter++ extension and are marked.
extreme_summary: Four 2025 stereo models add a strong monocular prior (Depth Anything V2) next to classical cost-volume matching, never in place of it. They inject it as extra features (FoundationStereo STA, DEFOM), as the starting disparity (DEFOM), or through a confidence-gated mutual refinement that first fits a global scale and shift of the prior to confident matches (MonSter). Fast-FoundationStereo then compresses the result about 10x with feature-level distillation, block-wise NAS and structured pruning.
task_definition: Dense disparity (inverse depth) for every pixel of a rectified stereo pair, zero-shot across domains. Mapping to Erudition: disparity maps to TVT level, pixel maps to MD column, and the left/right images map to lateral GR and typewell GR. The monocular prior maps to any estimate of TVT that does not come from GR matching.
inputs: Left and right RGB images. The frozen Depth Anything V2 (DINOv2 ViT) monocular depth network sees the left image. In our analogue the independent prior sources would be the particle-filter track (Ruby's 7.35 ft PF), the 2nd-place AnchorCNN+DP path, the XY geo prior / neighbour wells, and a trajectory-plus-constant-dip extrapolation from the known heel prefix.
target_parameterisation: Disparity in pixels. The monocular prior is relative inverse depth up to an unknown scale and shift. DEFOM normalises it (d0 = eta*w*z/max(z)) and then learns per-pixel multiplicative scale updates. MonSter fits one global scale and shift by least squares, then learns a per-pixel residual shift. The TVT analogue of the scale/shift ambiguity is a per-well offset plus a per-well slope along MD. That is exactly the 'one straight-line drift per well' error mode.
output_representation: Point disparity map. FoundationStereo builds a cost volume, gets an initial disparity by soft-argmin, then refines it with ConvGRU iterations. DEFOM and MonSter are RAFT/IGEV-style iterative refiners. Uncertainty is not a first-class output, though MonSter computes an internal confidence.
architecture: FoundationStereo: a side-tuning adapter (STA). A frozen DepthAnythingV2 feature is taken before its output head, reduced with a 4x4 stride-4 conv and concatenated with a same-scale CNN feature at 1/4 resolution. The adapter beat both direct ViT pyramid use and bidirectional feature exchange. Next comes a cost volume. Attentive Hybrid Cost Filtering (AHCF) follows: a 3D hourglass built from Axial-Planar Convolutions, which split a 3x3x3 conv into a spatial Ks x Ks x 1 conv and a disparity-only 1x1xKd conv, plus a Disparity Transformer that runs self-attention along the disparity axis of the cost volume. Last are soft-argmin init and coarse-to-fine ConvGRU refinement, about 0.7 s per 375x1242 image on an A100. DEFOM-Stereo builds on RAFT-Stereo. Its matching and context encoders fuse CNN features with Depth Anything V2 features through a trainable DPT head. The recurrent disparity starts from the normalised monocular depth, and a scale update module (a ConvGRU that predicts dense scale maps, d_n = s * d_{n-1}) runs a 'scale lookup' that samples correlation at a set of scale factors, giving global rather than local search. It costs +67% parameters and +42% runtime over RAFT-Stereo with ViT-L. MonSter has two branches. The mono branch is DepthAnythingV2; the stereo branch is IGEV-like. After N1 (about 2) stereo iterations, mono inverse depth is aligned to stereo disparity by a global least-squares scale and shift. Then N2 (about 2) rounds of mutual refinement follow. SGA (Stereo-Guided Alignment) uses confident stereo cues to estimate a per-pixel residual shift for the mono prior. MGR (Mono-Guided Refinement) uses the aligned mono disparity to fix stereo in ill-posed regions. Fast-FoundationStereo uses a single efficient student backbone in place of the hybrid ViT+CNN. Its cost-filtering blocks come from block-wise NAS solved with integer linear programming under a latency budget, and its ConvGRU refiner is pruned structurally along recurrent dependency graphs with first-order Taylor importance. It runs in 49 ms, or 21 ms with TensorRT, against 496 ms for the teacher.
core_mechanism: (1) The prior is a second, independent source of evidence that is strongest exactly where matching is ill-posed: occlusions, textureless and repetitive regions. Repeated rock layers are our version of a repetitive texture. (2) The prior is added, not substituted. The matching path still owns fine detail, and the prior is fused through features, initialisation or confidence-weighted refinement. (3) Scale ambiguity of the prior is resolved against the matcher. MonSter fits a global scale/shift to confident stereo pixels, then learns only local residuals. DEFOM learns multiplicative scale corrections with a global scale lookup. (4) The confidence gate means the prior only overrides matching where matching is unreliable. MonSter's confidence comes from the feature-warping residual |F_L(x) - F_R(x - D)|. (5) Global reasoning along the disparity axis, via FoundationStereo's Disparity Transformer, lets the network compare distant candidate disparities directly. This is the stereo analogue of comparing two repeated bands tens of levels apart, which local convolutions cannot see in one receptive field. (6) Fast-FoundationStereo shows that feature-level distillation, not only output supervision, carries much of the teacher's generalisation into a small student.
training_objective: FoundationStereo: smooth-L1 on the initial soft-argmin disparity plus exponentially weighted L1 over the GRU iterations, trained on its 1M-pair synthetic FSD dataset. An iterative self-curation loop drops and regenerates samples on which the model's BP-2 exceeds 60% (ambiguous or unlearnable). DEFOM and MonSter: RAFT/IGEV-style sequence L1 losses with gamma = 0.9 weighting. Fast-FoundationStereo: MSE between student and frozen-teacher backbone pyramid features, with each NAS block trained by distillation, then output-level training on synthetic data plus 1.4M pseudo-labelled internet stereo pairs. Pseudo-labels are filtered by agreement with monocular depth, normal-map consistency and sky masking.
decoding: FoundationStereo initialises with soft-argmin (the expectation over disparity) and then refines by regression. DEFOM and MonSter output the last refinement iterate as a point estimate. None of them decode a distribution at the end.
metric_consistent_decode: Partly. The soft-argmin init is the posterior mean (L2-consistent), but the final GRU regression under L1 loss is pulled toward a median-like, L1-optimal estimate. For our pooled RMSE, only the prior-fusion ideas transfer. The decode should stay the expectation over our per-column softmax.
evidence_scope: Whole image jointly. The monocular prior is global per image, and the cost volume is local per pixel plus aggregation. In our analogue the prior (PF / DP / geo) spans the whole lateral.
prefix_conditioning: Not applicable in stereo. In our analogue the known heel prefix is the natural anchor for MonSter's global scale/shift fit: fit the prior's offset and slope to the prefix labels and to the high-confidence U-Net columns, then pass only residuals to the network. This overlaps with item B10.
propose_vs_select: Fusion, not selection. The prior enters as features or initialisation, and a learned confidence decides where it dominates. It is not a candidate-plus-gate design. That matters here because our learned per-point gates between ConvNeXt and AnchorCNN already failed, while warm-started feature-level fusion has not been tried.
physical_constraints: Monocular depth carries object-level geometric plausibility. MonSter's global scale/shift is a two-parameter structural constraint, and its per-pixel residual is learned. The TVT analogue is a structural constraint of offset plus slope (a constant dip) per well, with learned local residuals.
dataset: FoundationStereo: FSD, 1M synthetic stereo pairs rendered in NVIDIA Omniverse, plus public synthetic sets. Fast-FoundationStereo adds 1.4M pseudo-labelled in-the-wild pairs. DEFOM and MonSter: SceneFlow and mixed datasets, evaluated zero-shot on KITTI 2012/2015, Middlebury and ETH3D.
synthetic_to_real: This is the headline claim of all four papers: training on synthetic data only, then zero-shot to real. FoundationStereo credits the frozen foundation features (STA) with closing the sim-to-real gap, and self-curation for removing ambiguous synthetic samples. Fast-FoundationStereo: pseudo-labelled real data moved RT-IGEV from 11.52% to 8.69% BP-2 on Middlebury-H. Relevance: Erudition trains on 85% synthetic wells. The pseudo-label lesson needs a large pool of unlabelled real wells, which we lack (data/test has 3 wells). The CLAUDE.md correction of 2026-09-21 already records this.
metric_and_performance: Fast-FoundationStereo: Middlebury-Q BP-2 2.12%, ETH3D BP-1 1.22%, KITTI-15 D1 3.25%, at 49 ms (21 ms TensorRT) against 496 ms for FoundationStereo. Backbone distillation ablation on Middlebury-H BP-2: 2.87% without to 2.20% with MSE feature distillation. DEFOM-Stereo, zero-shot from SceneFlow: about 13% error reduction on KITTI-12, more than 50% on Middlebury Bad-2.0 and 28% on ETH3D against RAFT-Stereo; first on several KITTI/Middlebury/ETH3D metrics at submission. MonSter: first on SceneFlow, KITTI-12/15, Middlebury and ETH3D, with up to 49.5% improvement in ETH3D Bad-1.0 over the previous best. MonSter++ reports SceneFlow EPE 0.37 against 0.47 for its IGEV baseline, and RT-MonSter++ runs at 47 ms at 1K resolution [uncertain] (these figures are from MonSter++, not the CVPR paper).
comparability: Not comparable numerically. These are image stereo benchmarks with bad-pixel or EPE metrics. Only the architectural and training recipes transfer to our pooled RMSE over 155 holdout wells.
validation_protocol: Standard stereo benchmarks with official held-out test servers (KITTI, Middlebury, ETH3D) and zero-shot cross-domain evaluation. There is no analogue of our spatial-leakage or test-picked-checkpoint issues.
inference_budget: FoundationStereo about 0.5-0.7 s per image on an A100. DEFOM +42% over RAFT-Stereo. Fast-FoundationStereo 21-49 ms. For us the relevant cost is only the extra prior channels or a small second stage: a few ms per well on the RTX 5060. The PF or AnchorCNN prior costs whatever it already costs. AnchorCNN+DP made the blend 5-6x slower in the earlier measurement, so a PF or geo prior is the budget-friendly source.
repeated_layers: In stereo, repetitive textures are a named failure case that the monocular prior resolves, because the prior does not depend on matching. The analogue for band confusion (about 51% of our squared error) is an independent absolute-position prior that is correct to within half a band spacing. When the prior is itself ambiguous, as the XY geo-prior hump-picking experiment found, fusion cannot help. The Disparity Transformer (attention along the disparity/level axis) is a second, prior-free mechanism: it lets the network compare repeated candidate bands globally.
drift: MonSter's global scale-and-shift alignment is structurally a per-image two-parameter fit. The TVT equivalent is a per-well offset plus slope, which matches the drift mode directly. Our posterior dump (results/baseline_check_posterior_all/posterior_report.json, 60-epoch baseline) shows that an oracle per-well straight-line removal would cut pooled RMSE from 5.47 to 3.30 ft, and a per-well offset removal gives 4.05 ft. The drift component is therefore large, and a confident anchor for that line could remove much of it.
uncertainty_and_calibration: MonSter uses a confidence estimate (the warping residual) to gate fusion. FoundationStereo and DEFOM do not output calibrated uncertainty. None report calibration. For us the useful point is the confidence gate: the prior should affect only columns where the U-Net posterior is broad or multimodal.
where_to_use: (a) As an input-side fusion. Feed an independent TVT prior as extra channels to the U-Net, following the DEFOM/FoundationStereo 'add alongside' pattern, warm-started from a trained checkpoint so the starved-training failure of rb_v1_neighbor does not repeat. (b) As a MonSter-lite second stage. Align the prior to the stage-1 posterior with a confidence-weighted per-well offset+slope fit, then have a small refiner take [stage-1 posterior, aligned prior, confidence] and output a corrected per-column softmax. (c) As an architectural block. Add a Disparity-Transformer-style attention along the level axis (not MD) inside the U-Net. (d) In the distillation step. Add feature-level MSE distillation from ConvNeXt-small to FastViT, per Fast-FoundationStereo, beyond the current output KL.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (about 51%) via an independent prior and level-axis attention; drift (about 25%) via confidence-weighted offset+slope alignment; distillation quality for the FastViT student.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already do: an independent prior as input exists in principle. rb_v1_neighbor added 9 geo-prior channels (16 to 24 inputs) but was starved (3.1x behind the baseline at 60 epochs) and never tested warm-started. The pf_v1 particle-filter channel is only planned. Output-level KD (KL at T=2, single or ensemble teacher) is built and works: FastViT-SA12 taught by ConvNeXt-small is the best single model at 4.84 ft. DINOv2 as a backbone replacement was correctly rejected (25x29 single-scale maps break the 2:1 resolution rule). What we do not do: (1) No confidence-gated fusion. Every prior use so far has been either a raw input channel trained from scratch, a post-hoc hump pick (geo pick) or a learned hard gate between models. None used MonSter's two-step 'fit the prior's global offset+slope on confident columns, then learn a residual' design. (2) No initialisation from a prior. The U-Net is one-shot, and the RAFT refiner (arch_v3) started from the network's own expectation, not from an independent prior. (3) No attention along the level axis. arch_v2_axial attended along MD. FoundationStereo's Disparity Transformer attends along disparity, the axis on which the repeated bands lie. At ConvNeXt stage 1 the level axis has 100 positions and at stage 2 it has 50, so this is cheap. (4) No axial-planar split of spatial and level kernels. arch_v4_lkconv was dead (zero-init deadlock) and never measured, so the anisotropic kernel idea is still untested. (5) Distillation is output-only. Fast-FoundationStereo's ablation credits backbone feature MSE with a 23% relative BP-2 gain (2.87% to 2.20%). (6) No self-curation of synthetic data. FoundationStereo regenerates synthetic samples the model finds unlearnable. We could audit which z_shift simulations produce truly unresolvable repeated-band cases. Whether to drop them (FoundationStereo) or keep them (calibration) is open. Keeping them is probably right under a mean decode.
proposed_experiment: E1, a MonSter-lite prior fusion that is warm-started and cheap. In experiments/arch (fork of 0801_V2): (i) produce a per-column independent prior from the AnchorCNN+DP holdout path if it is cached, otherwise from the PF; (ii) compute a confidence-weighted per-well offset+slope alignment of that prior to the stage-1 expectation, weighting columns by 1/posterior-variance restricted to unimodal columns and including the heel prefix where labels are known; (iii) render the aligned prior as a Gaussian 'prior plane' over the 400 levels with width equal to its residual std, plus a scalar confidence plane, giving 2 extra input channels; (iv) extend the U-Net's input projection (the to_backbone 1x1 conv) with zero-initialised weights for the new channels so the model is bit-identical at init, then fine-tune from results/cnx_tiny_ep150 for 30-40 epochs. Touch seq_NN_dataset.py (new channels), seq_NN_models.py (input width and zero-init; register in model_named_parameters), seq_NN_cfg.py (recipe arch_v5_prior_fuse). Control: the identical fine-tune schedule from the same checkpoint with the new channels filled with zeros. This removes the extra-epochs confound; the noise floor is ±0.39 ft per single run, so use seq_NN_robust_compare.py and two seeds per arm, and report the SSE change split by posterior_analysis.py categories (wrong_mode, blend, unimodal_offset). E2, level-axis attention: add a Disparity-Transformer-style block (gated residual, zero-init gamma, like AxialMDStack but transposed to attend over W=level with MD positions folded into the batch) after ConvNeXt stages 1-2 (level 100/50 positions). Recipe arch_v6_level_attn, 150 epochs; the control is cnx_tiny_ep150. Verify identity at init and live gradients on both gate and weights, given the lkconv lesson. E3, feature-level KD: in seq_NN_train.py add an MSE loss between 1x1-projected FastViT decoder features and frozen ConvNeXt-small decoder features at 2-3 U-Net scales (weight about 0.1 of the KL term), alongside the existing distill_alignment_loss. Recipe cnx_fastvit_kd_small_feat; the control is cnx_fastvit_kd_small_ep150.
implementation_effort: E1 medium: a new prior pipeline plus dataset channels, but the zero-init warm-start pattern already exists in experiments/arch. E2 low-medium: it mirrors AxialMDStack with the axes swapped. E3 low: a forward hook on decoder features plus 1x1 projection heads.
gpu_cost: E1: a 30-40 epoch fine-tune of tiny at about 65-110 s per epoch is about 1 h per arm, so about 4 h for 2 seeds x 2 arms, plus prior generation (PF on CPU). E2: a full 150-epoch run (about 5 h) or a 40-epoch warm start (about 1.2 h). Attention over 100 level positions x 173 MD positions x batch fits in 8 GB. E3: about 2 h 40 min per 150-epoch FastViT run plus teacher forward passes (already paid by the current KD).
distillation_compatibility: Good. E1's prior channels and E2's block are part of the student's inputs and architecture, so a FastViT student can include them and the output-posterior KD stays unchanged. E3 is itself a distillation upgrade. Feature KD needs 1x1 adapters because FastViT and ConvNeXt channel widths differ.
error_correlation_with_ours: An independent prior (PF or DP) has different errors from GR-matching U-Nets. AnchorCNN blends showed that diversity exists, but a learned gate could not exploit it. Fusion at the feature level inside the network is the stereo field's answer to exactly this problem. A level-attention variant of the same U-Net would correlate highly (about 0.85, like the other ConvNeXt variants), so as an ensemble member it adds only seed-style diversity.
risk: (1) The prior may not be informative where it matters. The XY geo prior failed at hump picking, and in stereo the monocular prior is strong because depth networks are trained on millions of images, while our PF/DP priors are much weaker (PF 7.35 ft against U-Net 4.8-5.2 ft). (2) Data-limited regime: extra channels trained from scratch starved rb_v1_neighbor. The warm-start plus zero-init plan addresses this, but the fine-tune may learn to ignore the channels. (3) Leakage: the AnchorCNN/PF prior for holdout wells must be produced without holdout labels and without holdout-picked checkpoints. The known caveat already inflates numbers by about 0.15 ft. (4) Level attention might repeat arch_v2's pattern, where gammas barely move in 60 epochs. Use 150 epochs or a warm start. (5) Effects below ±0.39 ft are unmeasurable on a single run. The accidental null draw produced k*=21 and 64% bootstrap with no model change.
notes: The CLAUDE.md survey (2026-09-21) already drew the right high-level lesson ('add alongside, never replace') and rejected DINOv2. This item adds the concrete mechanisms that were not yet mapped. First, MonSter's global scale/shift followed by a learned residual maps onto a per-well offset+slope, and the posterior dump shows a per-well line-removal oracle of 3.30 ft against 5.47. Second, FoundationStereo's Disparity Transformer is attention along the level axis, which differs from the MD-axial attention already tested. Third, Fast-FoundationStereo's clearest distillation lever is feature-level MSE, not output KL alone. The pseudo-labelling lesson does not apply (no unlabelled real wells), and self-curation is ambiguous under a mean decode. Ambiguous synthetic samples teach correct uncertainty, so do not drop them blindly.
